claims.text: An ML framework integrating high-throughput computational data with disorder-sensitive descriptors can predict low phonon thermal conductivity in high-entropy alloys more accurately than conventional DFT or classical MD.
The target materials are multi-principal-element, disordered solid-solution high-entropy alloys under thermal-insulation operating conditions.
The ML model will be trained using both high-throughput simulation data and experimental measurements.
The model will incorporate descriptors representing compositional complexity and local lattice distortions.
Integrating high-throughput computation, modeling, and experimental validation is useful for accelerating high-entropy-alloy discovery.
The model is intended for composition and temperature ranges typical of thermal-insulation applications where disorder is characterized and the alloy remains a stable, single-phase disordered state.
Intrinsic atomic disorder and local lattice distortions enhance phonon scattering in high-entropy alloys.
Nonlinear relationships connect high-dimensional compositional and microstructural descriptors to phonon-scattering mechanisms.
Capturing those nonlinear relationships will allow the ML model to map the influence of disorder on thermal transport more accurately.
The ML framework will reduce phonon-thermal-conductivity prediction error by 20–30% relative to conventional DFT or MD.
The resulting improvement will allow better identification of high-entropy alloys having low phonon thermal conductivity.
Standard DFT and classical MD do not adequately account for the disorder and configurational complexity of high-entropy alloys.
The approach will be reliable only for high-entropy alloys with significant configurational disorder and without substantial local ordering or phase separation.
Prediction accuracy may deteriorate outside the model's calibrated composition and temperature ranges.
The magnitude of improvement will depend on the quality and range of the high-throughput data and on the selected disorder-sensitive descriptors.
A decisive benchmark will compare ML, DFT, and MD predictions against standardized experimental phonon thermal conductivity measurements for the same high-entropy-alloy dataset.
Failure to reduce prediction error by at least 20% relative to conventional DFT or MD will falsify the hypothesis.
Absence of a statistically significant correlation between disorder-sensitive descriptors and measured phonon thermal conductivity will falsify the hypothesis.
